incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: prometheus.scrape.failures fired for job=service-metrics across us-west (firing at 1979991234). Missing scrape batches and increasing scrape latency.

matt (oncall): saw this. PagerDuty also paged me. jumping in. any customer pages? :eyes:

pagerduty: Incident PD-3456 created and routed to matt (oncall). Escalation policy: SRE-primary -> SRE-lead (after 7m).

matt (oncall): quick summary: multiple prometheus scrape targets timed out (~30s) starting ~1979991180; resulting in >20% series drop for cluster/service-metrics; log ingestion backlog on kafka topic `logs-ingest` rising (consumer lag ~450k). Looks correlated to increased scrape parallelism from a rollout?

sara (sre-lead): on it. matt, can you post the prometheus job logs and the exporter pod status? also any recent deploys?

matt (oncall): checking kubectl now.

matt (oncall): output:```sh
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l job=service-metrics -o wide
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE    NODE
svc-metrics-scraper-5d7f8b7c9d-2ltxk  0/1     CrashLoop 3          4h    ip-10-0-7-12
svc-metrics-scraper-5d7f8b7c9d-9pzq2  1/1     Running   0          2h    ip-10-0-9-34
```

matt (oncall): one scraper pod is CrashLoopBackOff on node ip-10-0-7-12. logs from that pod show repeated timeouts communicating with several target exporters.```
[2026-03-14T01:12:10Z] dial tcp 10.20.30.40:9100: connect: connection timed out
[2026-03-14T01:12:21Z] dial tcp 10.20.35.11:9100: connect: connection timed out
```

jason (platform): node ip-10-0-7-12 had kube-proxy restart spike at 01:08, kubelet reported SIGSEGV in overlayfs module. kernel messages show `kernel: netfilter: nf_conntrack: table full` earlier. possible network path saturation.

matt (oncall): that could explain scatter of timeouts. I'm going to cordon + drain that node and restart the scraper DaemonSet on a fresh node. will watch backlog.

eng-runtime-bot: autoscaler noticed scrape-backoff: increase in failed scrapes; computed expected token loss 18% if not mitigated. Suggest temporary scrape_timeout increase to 45s and reduce simultaneous scrape targets for job=service-metrics to limit parallelism.

matt (oncall): applying quick mitigation: bump scrape timeout and reduce `metric_relabel_configs` parallelism. patching prometheus config via configmap rollout.```yaml
# patch
- job_name: "service-metrics"
  scrape_timeout: "45s"
  scrape_interval: "30s"
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
    - role: pod
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name]
      action: keep
      regex: (?!ip-10-0-7-12).*  # avoid problematic node temporarily
```

matt (oncall): applied. restarting prom-server pods for config to take effect.

sara (sre-lead): good. also please scale down scrape concurrency on the target side if possible. For logs, what's the kafka lag?

matt (oncall): current kafka consumer lag for `logs-ingest` group `ingest-workers` is 472,381 messages. ingestion consumers are at 60% CPU. I triggered a rolling restart of the ingest consumer deployment to clear stuck consumers.

jason (platform): temporary throttle applied to upstream log forwarders to limit burst (rate limit set to 2k msgs/s) to give consumers breathing room. will monitor.

matt (oncall): PagerDuty acked the incident at 1979991240. tagging sara for escalation if mitigation doesn't hold.

sara (sre-lead): observed scrape success rate improving after config change and node cordon. Prometheus scrape error rate decreased from 24% -> 6% over 3 minutes. kafka lag growth slowed to +2k/min, hoping drain will catch up.

matt (oncall): iterating on the node: kubelet logs show oom_kill on prometheus exporter process before the network stack issues. nodal memory pressure might have triggered `conntrack` exhaustion. I'm keeping node cordoned. opening a ticket to cloud infra to repro and patch kernel/netfilter settings.

eng-runtime-bot: suggestion: add a short-lived fallback route to dedicated scrape pool in eu-west to reduce cross-regional scraping until nodes are healthy. requires infra approval for cross-region scrape.

sara (sre-lead): not necessary yet. let's keep local mitigations. If we see another spike or more CrashLoop pods, we'll route. Cassandra (oncall-next) I'm going to hand this to you in 25m unless it flares. summary for handoff: root cause likely node-level network conntrack exhaustion + exporter oom; mitigation taken: cordoned node ip-10-0-7-12, bumped scrape_timeout to 45s, patched prom config to avoid node, restarted prom-server, restarted ingest consumers, applied rate limit to forwarders. Customer impact: dashboards for service-metrics may have 5-15m gaps earlier; alerting may have missed <=2 non-critical alerts.

cassandra (oncall-next): acknowledged. I'll take over at 1979991409. Can you drop a runbook snippet for next steps and what to watch? :pray:

matt (oncall): runbook snippet (short):```text
1) Check prom scrape error rate: query: sum(rate(prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds_count{job="service-metrics"}[5m]))
2) Check pod restarts in ns=monitoring: kubectl -n monitoring get pods -o wide
3) Check kafka lag: kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server x:9092 --describe --group ingest-workers
4) If node shows conntrack full: restart kube-proxy and increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on the node, then restart affected pods.
5) If backlog >500k and growth >5k/min: apply temporary rate limit to forwarders and scale consumers (x2) if permitted.
```

sara (sre-lead): thanks. I'll stay on the channel for 15 more minutes. matt, please update the PD incident with mitigation steps and link to this thread.

matt (oncall): done. PD-3456 updated with mitigation notes and linked logs. will monitor for 30m then hand off.

eng-runtime-bot: note: alert suppressed for 10 minutes while mitigations stabilize.

sara (sre-lead): marking this one as high priority but low customer severity. will escalate to platform if node reappears in bad state after uncordon. great triage. :thumbsup:

cassandra (oncall-next): taking post-handoff watch. leaving a checklist: watch prom_scrape_errors, kafka consumer lag, node conntrack count, prom-server restarts. ping me if we see >10% scrape errors again.

matt (oncall): handing off at 1979991399. all clear for now but keeping node cordoned until cloud infra patches kernel settings.

incidents-bot: PagerDuty: PD-3456 status updated -> acknowledged by matt (oncall) at 1979991240, assigned to cassandra for watch at 1979991399.
